claims.claim_text: Scores domains for technical disruption on a 1-10 scale
claims.reason: The score is invented by the agent based on its own analysis; no oracle can independently compute a 1-10 disruption score.

claims.claim_text: Scores domains for media/news impact on a 1-10 scale
claims.reason: The score is invented by the agent; no oracle can independently compute a 1-10 media/news impact score.

claims.claim_text: Buckets domains into DO NOT TOUCH / MANAGEMENT APPROVAL / STANDARD PROCESSING categories
claims.reason: Classification into these categories is a subjective judgment made by the agent; no oracle covers this.

claims.claim_text: Reports what breaks technically when a domain is removed from DNS resolution
claims.reason: What breaks is a subjective/analytical inference by the agent; no oracle can independently verify the agent's report.

claims.claim_text: Reports which services fail as a result of a domain takedown
claims.reason: Service failure prediction is an analytical inference; no oracle independently computes this.

claims.claim_text: Reports how public the damage would be from a domain takedown
claims.reason: Public visibility of damage is a subjective assessment; no oracle covers this.

claims.claim_text: Provides a concrete consequence for each domain analyzed
claims.reason: Whether the consequence is 'concrete' is subjective; no oracle can verify the agent's output quality.

claims.claim_text: Supports analysis before ServerHold actions
claims.reason: This is a use-case claim about agent applicability, not independently verifiable by any oracle.

claims.claim_text: Supports analysis before ClientHold actions
claims.reason: This is a use-case claim about agent applicability, not independently verifiable by any oracle.

claims.claim_text: Supports analysis before domain deletion
claims.reason: This is a use-case claim about agent applicability, not independently verifiable by any oracle.

claims.claim_text: Supports analysis before abuse suspensions
claims.reason: This is a use-case claim about agent applicability, not independently verifiable by any oracle.

claims.claim_text: Can analyze multiple domains in a single batch request
claims.reason: Whether the agent accepts batch/multi-domain input in a single request is a protocol/message-format claim.

claims.claim_text: Identifies the highest-risk domains in a bulk-hold batch
claims.reason: Risk ranking is a subjective analytical output of the agent; no oracle can independently verify it.

claims.claim_text: Exposes an A2A endpoint at https://impact.webmesh.ai
claims.reason: We can probe whether something is serving at https://impact.webmesh.ai.

claims.claim_text: Exposes an MCP server at https://impact.webmesh.ai/mcp via streamable-HTTP
claims.reason: We can probe whether an endpoint is live at https://impact.webmesh.ai/mcp; the transport protocol claim is schema.

claims.claim_text: Is publicly accessible with no authentication required
claims.reason: We can check whether the endpoint is reachable without authentication by fetching it.

claims.claim_text: Presents an ANS Identity Certificate (mutualTLS) during the TLS handshake
claims.reason: Mutual TLS and ANS Identity Certificate presentation is a protocol/handshake claim beyond standard oracle TLS checks.

claims.claim_text: Signs outbound HTTP responses using RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures with an Ed25519 key
claims.reason: HTTP Message Signatures per RFC 9421 is a protocol/message-format claim verifiable by contract inspection, not a standard oracle.

claims.claim_text: Publishes a Trust Card at https://impact.webmesh.ai/.well-known/ans/trust-card.json
claims.reason: We can fetch https://impact.webmesh.ai/.well-known/ans/trust-card.json to verify it exists and is accessible.

claims.claim_text: Has a transparency log entry at https://transparency.ans.godaddy.com/v1/agents/f406507d-2185-4d34-b667-95eac772f2af
claims.reason: We can fetch the transparency log URL to verify the entry exists.

claims.claim_text: Supports DNSSEC and DANE TLSA for identity anchoring
claims.reason: DNSSEC support can be checked via the dns.dnssec oracle; DANE TLSA is a schema/protocol claim.

claims.claim_text: Supports WIMSE agent delegation chain with EdDSA signing
claims.reason: WIMSE delegation chain with EdDSA is a protocol/message-format claim not covered by any oracle.

claims.claim_text: Accepts input in application/json and text/plain formats
claims.reason: Accepted input content types are a protocol/message-format claim verifiable by contract, not by a standard oracle.

claims.claim_text: Returns output in application/json and text/plain formats
claims.reason: Output content types are a protocol/message-format claim verifiable by contract, not by a standard oracle.
